forecast-period.text: A high pressure system located to the south of SA will maintain a ridge over the state as it moves into the Tasman Sea from late Wednesday. A trough ahead of a strong cold front is then expected move over western SA on Thursday, before the front tracks east across the rest of SA on Friday and early Saturday. A high will quickly move southeast across the state on Saturday, ahead of another front forecast to move across on Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy early morning frost about the southeast. Dry. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to above average in the southwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh in the northeast during the day.
Dry. Slight chance of an isolated light shower about the northern agricultural area. South to southeasterly winds.

Dry in the east. Showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west from the afternoon and extending into central districts overnight. Thunderstorms may be severe with damaging wind gusts possible west of about Ceduna. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, freshening about the coast and in the west during the day.

Showers and thunderstorms moving east across much of the state, clearing from the west later. Thunderstorms may be severe with damaging wind gusts possible about central parts. Maximum temperatures near to above average in the east, tending below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds, ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending across the state throughout the day. Winds freshening about northern and western inland areas, and about the coast with the change.

text.p: Showers about the agricultural areas and adjacent districts, mostly clearing by the afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms possible early across the north and northeast. Maximum temperatures below average. West to southwesterly winds. Winds from the evening tend light about the agricultural areas and southeast to northeasterly elsewhere.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Less than 2 mm in the north, broadly increasing to 2 to 10 mm elsewhere. Falls increasing further to 5 to 15 mm across the agricultural areas, with possible isolated totals between 15 to 25 mm.
